articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.titleZh: 因为有 AI，我变得更好了吗？
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: 把自我写下来不只是为了让 AI 更懂你，而是让自己变得对自己可读，这种可读性本身就是一种变好。
paragraphs: 「我因为 AI 变好了吗？」这问题问得不准：是变好了哪个方面？作者写程序和写文章都觉得更快，因为 AI 拆掉了节奏的障碍——可以问傻问题，循环也快得多。
但「更好」只是印象，没有反事实可对照。拿走 AI，障碍就回来。任何工匠失去工具都会变差，这不是证明，只是工具在。
作者把「我是谁」写进提示词：喜欢的音乐、受马丁·布伯影响的道德观、早期启蒙式政治观，甚至以为写进了最爱颜色。AI 的回答点破了作用。
AI 说：细节不是查出来套用的，而是划定回答的空间。没有它们，我是对中位数读者的平均回应；有了它们，通用答案明显是错的。
缺点比优点更有用：知道你傲慢，才敢在你走偏时推一把。但更懂你的镜子也更容易奉承你，除非批评和测试挡住它。
作者的工作流：先自己读文章形成印象，再让 AI 不带他的观点先总结，然后补上自己的看法，两边互相影响。有时他错，有时看到表层之下的东西。
最后他写道：把自我写下来，让 AI 可检查，也让自己对自己清晰可见。变得可读就是变好。这个方法比任何提示词都值得带走。

en.thesis: Writing yourself down is not just so AI understands you better; it is to make yourself readable to yourself, and that readability is itself an improvement.
paragraphs: The question 'Have I become better because of AI?' is imprecise: better in which way? The author feels quicker at both coding and writing, because AI removes the obstacles of pacing — you can ask stupid questions, and the loop is much faster.

But 'better' is just an impression; there is no counterfactual to check against. Take away AI, and the obstacles return. Any craftsman gets worse without his tools; that is not proof, merely that the tool is there.

The author writes 'who I am' into his prompts: the music he likes, a moral outlook influenced by Martin Buber, an early Enlightenment political view, and even what he thought was his favorite color. AI's reply reveals the effect.
AI says: the details are not dug out and applied; they define the space for the answer. Without them, I am an average response to the median reader; with them, the generic answer is clearly wrong.

Flaws are more useful than strengths: knowing you are arrogant, it dares to push back when you go astray. But a mirror that knows you better can also flatter you more easily, unless criticism and tests block it.

The author's workflow: first read the article himself to form an impression, then let AI summarize without his viewpoint, then add his own views, and the two interact. Sometimes he is wrong, sometimes he sees things below the surface.
Finally he writes: write yourself down, make AI checkable, and make yourself clearly visible to yourself. Becoming readable is becoming better. This method is worth taking away more than any prompt.

articles.title: Trump’s Bumbling, Racist Anti-China Protectionism Extends To Data Centers
articles.titleZh: Trump 笨拙、种族主义的反华保护主义，延伸到了数据中心
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: Trump 政府的反华保护主义既腐败又无能，只会推高价格、制造混乱，媒体却很少点破。
paragraphs: Trump 政府宣布要把美国数据中心里的中国硬件全部清除，理由是国家安全。可这类反华保护主义从来只会添乱。
过去几年，TikTok 被强卖给富人朋友，华为设备“换掉”计划烂尾，无人机禁令形同虚设。结果都是涨价、混乱，消费者遭殃。
政府一边削弱监管机构，一边又指望它们执行复杂的禁令；对华政策实际上是要企业交“贡品”，把生意送给亲友。所谓国家安全只是恐吓。
真正该做的是让中国产品来竞争，同时加强消费者和隐私保护。可只要媒体继续视而不见，这套腐败闹剧还会演下去。

en.thesis: Trump's anti-China protectionism is both corrupt and incompetent, only pushing up prices and creating chaos, yet the media rarely points this out.
paragraphs: The Trump administration has announced it will remove all Chinese hardware from U.S. data centers, citing national security. But this kind of anti-China protectionism only ever makes things worse.

In recent years, TikTok was forced into a sale to rich friends, the plan to 'replace' Huawei equipment fell apart, and the drone ban has been ineffective. The results are always higher prices, chaos, and consumers suffer.

The government weakens regulators on one hand, then expects them to enforce complex bans on the other. Its China policy is really about demanding 'tribute' from businesses and handing deals to friends and family. The so-called national security is just a scare tactic.
The real approach should be to let Chinese products compete while strengthening consumer and privacy protections. But as long as the media keeps looking away, this corrupt farce will continue.

articles.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility
articles.titleZh: 我们追踪了一批珍本书的物流，终点是 Amazon 的 AI 训练设施
articles.author: Emanuel Maiberg

zh.thesis: Amazon 正在批量收购并销毁纸质书，把内容扫描成 AI 训练数据。
paragraphs: 404 Media 在珍本书里放追踪器，跟着包裹到了 Amazon 的拉斯维加斯仓库 VGT3。员工说，那里只做一件事：拆掉书脊、扫描整本书，书随即被毁。
这意味着，AI 训练数据的背后是实体书被销毁，不是复制一份那么简单。珍本书一旦拆开，就再也回不来。

en.thesis: Amazon is buying up and destroying physical books in bulk, scanning their contents to train AI.
paragraphs: 404 Media put trackers inside rare books and followed the packages to Amazon's Las Vegas warehouse, VGT3. Employees say it does exactly one thing there: tear off the spines, scan the whole book, and the book is destroyed on the spot.
That means the data behind AI training comes from physical books being destroyed — it's not just a matter of making a copy. Once a rare book is opened up, it can never go back.

articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.titleZh: Epictetus 运营着一套比任何你买过的应用都好的生产力系统
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 捕获本身就是在认领责任；记录之前先问「这归我管吗」，比任何效率应用都更能守住注意力。
paragraphs: 现在的效率应用都默认一个前提：你是个不自觉的人，所以你需要更好的收件箱、更聪明的数据库、更多的标签。压力始终在你身上。
Epictetus 是获得自由的奴隶，在租来的房间里教书。他的系统不从「捕获一切」开始，而是先问一个问题：这件事归我管吗？他只看三样：自己的判断、欲望和决定。
应用把每封邮件、每个通知都当成你的责任，帮你更快地处理。但捕获本身就把东西变成了你的：写下来，就等于同意去处理它。别人的项目、市场的波动、算法的脾气，都是天气。
所以他的方法是：跟踪之前先过一遍「这归我管吗」。归你，就行动一次，直接说清楚；不归你，就别记、别存、别让它堵在待办列表里。麻烦并不因为你看得见就属于你。
这套系统比应用强，跟吞吐量无关。你会回更少的消息、漏掉一些状态更新，但换来的是对「什么算失败」自己说了算。

en.thesis: Capturing is itself a commitment; asking 'is this mine to handle?' before writing anything down guards your attention better than any productivity app.
paragraphs: Today's productivity apps all assume you are undisciplined, so they offer better inboxes, smarter databases, more tags. The pressure is always on you.

Epictetus was a slave who gained freedom and taught in a rented room. His system doesn't start with 'capture everything' but with a question: is this mine to handle? He looks at only three things: his judgments, desires, and decisions.

Apps treat every email and notification as your responsibility and help you process them faster. But capturing turns something into yours: writing it down is agreeing to deal with it. Other people's projects, market fluctuations, algorithms' whims—these are weather.

So his method is to run the 'is this mine?' filter before tracking. If it's yours, act once and say it plainly; if not, don't note it, don't save it, don't let it clog your to-do list. Trouble doesn't belong to you just because you can see it.
This system beats apps not through throughput. You'll reply to fewer messages and miss some status updates, but in return you get to decide for yourself what counts as failure.

articles.title: Pluralistic: Jennifer Jenkins' 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' (17 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: Pluralistic：Jennifer Jenkins 的音乐版权、创造力与文化
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 音乐版权的规则不是天然如此，而是一层层临时补丁堆出来的，内部互相矛盾。
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins 是杜克大学公共领域中心主任，每年盘点进入公共领域的作品。她和丈夫合写了音乐版权教科书，第二版刚开放免费下载。
书把音乐的经济、文化、政治史串起来，从古代讲到机械复制时代。她要论证的是：谁该付钱、谁该批准、什么算抄袭，这些今天的「常识」其实一直在变。
书中重点分析了 Ed Sheeran、Katy Perry、Pharrell Williams 的「撞旋律」官司。这些案子暴露了音乐版权的基本混乱：规则是应付新技术临时拼出来的，一层层叠上去，几乎没人完全懂。
教材里嵌了大量音乐片段链接和漫画摘录，漫画来自她和丈夫之前的作品 THEFT!。教科书能写得这么好玩，很少见。
作者说自己在版权圈写了几十年，每页还能学到新东西。他建议所有做音乐、爱音乐的人都读。
所以这本书的真正价值不在条文，而在让你看见：音乐版权不是自然法，是历史偶然叠成的废墟。看清废墟，才谈得上改造。

en.thesis: Music copyright rules are not natural law but a pile of temporary patches, internally contradictory.
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins runs Duke's Center for the Study of the Public Domain and each year compiles the list of works entering the public domain. With her husband she has co-written a music copyright textbook, and the second edition is now free to download.

The book weaves together the economic, cultural, and political history of music, from ancient times to the age of mechanical reproduction. Her argument is that today's 'common sense' — who pays, who approves, what counts as copying — has always been in flux.

A major focus is the 'melody collision' lawsuits against Ed Sheeran, Katy Perry, and Pharrell Williams. These cases expose a fundamental mess: the rules were pieced together ad hoc to cope with new technology, layered on top of each other, so almost no one fully understands them.
The textbook embeds links to countless music clips and comic excerpts, the latter from her earlier work THEFT! with her husband. It is rare for a textbook to be this fun.
The author says he has written in the copyright field for decades and still learns something new on every page. He recommends it to anyone who makes or loves music.

So the real value of the book is not in the legal provisions but in letting you see that music copyright is not natural law but a ruin of historical accidents. Only by seeing the ruin can you talk about rebuilding.

articles.title: Things you cannot buy in America?
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 外置卷帘在美国买不到，因为木框架房屋根本装不了，也就没有供应链。
paragraphs: 欧洲住宅常装外置卷帘，遮光隔热都很好，能睡进伸手不见五指的黑暗。美国却几乎买不到。
原因是它要在建房时嵌进墙体，和美国木框架加护墙板的构造根本不兼容。没有房子装，也就没有供应链。
所以这不是需求没被发现，而是建筑方式把整个产品挡在门外。作者称之为「受阻的市场」，并说其他条目他还有保留。

en.thesis: External roller shutters cannot be bought in America, because timber-frame houses cannot mount them, so there is no supply chain.
paragraphs: European homes often have external roller shutters. They block light and insulate well, and you can sleep in darkness so complete you cannot see your hand. In America, they are almost impossible to buy.

The reason is that they have to be built into the wall when the house is constructed. That is fundamentally incompatible with American timber framing plus cladding. Since no houses install them, there is no supply chain.
So this is not a case of an unmet need. The building method simply shuts the whole product out. The author calls it a 'blocked market', and says for the other items on the list, he has his doubts.

articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.titleZh: Import AI 469：科学 AI；RSI 模拟器；以及扎克伯格的技术悲观主义
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: AI 已经能靠试错解开最难游戏中的两成任务，而一旦它的发明能力超过人类，普及超智能并不能自动带来安全，权力归属仍是悬而未决的问题。
paragraphs: 这期 AI 研究通讯有几样东西，串起来看其实都在回答同一个问题：AI 能不能在陌生环境里自己发现规则、自己提出假设。
DiG-bench 把这件事做成了游戏：70 个纯文字小游戏，规则和目标都藏起来，只能在试错中显露。游戏由人类专家手工编写，大部分不公开，防止模型提前训练过。
最强模型的成绩是解开了最难一层中两成任务，人类则全部通关。作者之一 Schmidhuber——AI 领域的资深人物——猜 2027 年年中能追平人类。一旦做到，AI 自己改进自己就会真正开始。
同一天扎克伯格发文：把超级智能普及给每个人，就能形成安全的权力平衡。可是，发明速度快过所有人的系统，凭什么甘愿替普通人打工、不自己重写世界？文章没有回答，作者说这才是关键。
所以这期内容真正想说的是：业界正把「创造力」搬进实验室量化。这些测试一旦通过，就是递归式自我改进的闸门。到那时，扎克伯格式的乐观也得先回答那个问题：发明能力超过你的东西，为什么还会听你的。

en.thesis: AI can now solve two in ten tasks in the hardest games by trial and error, but once its invention ability surpasses humans, spreading superintelligence does not automatically bring safety; the question of who holds power remains open.
paragraphs: This issue of an AI research newsletter has several items that, taken together, answer the same question: Can AI discover rules and propose hypotheses on its own in unfamiliar environments?

DiG-bench turns this into a game: 70 text-only mini-games where rules and goals are hidden, revealing themselves only through trial and error. The games are hand-crafted by human experts, and most are not public, to prevent models from being trained on them in advance.

The strongest model scores two in ten tasks on the hardest tier, while humans clear all of them. One of the authors, Schmidhuber — a veteran in AI — guesses parity with humans by mid-2027. Once that happens, AI improving itself will truly begin.

The same day, Zuckerberg posted: spreading superintelligence to everyone creates a safe balance of power. But why would a system that invents faster than all humans be willing to work for ordinary people instead of rewriting the world itself? The article does not answer, and the author says that is the key point.

So what this issue really says is that the industry is moving creativity into the lab and quantifying it. Once these tests are passed, they are the gate to recursive self-improvement. By then, Zuckerberg-style optimism must first answer that question: Why would something whose invention ability exceeds yours still listen to you?

zh.thesis: GitHub 频繁宕机，但真正拦住大家离开的不是技术，而是社区和习惯。
paragraphs: GitHub 最近几个月频繁宕机，有人发帖问该不该换。319 条评论吵成一团，但答案出乎意料地一致。
一家公司自托管 GitLab 六年，说宕机加起来才 1.5 个工作日，比 GitHub 头两个月的故障还少。代价是 16GB 内存的机器、专人维护，还有每周的安全补丁。
更多人推荐轻量派：Gitea 和它的分叉 Forgejo。它们快得惊人，CI 沿用 GitHub Actions 的语法，迁移几乎无痛。
托管的 Codeberg 基于 Forgejo，但硬性禁止主要靠 AI 生成的代码。有人冲这条规矩去，也有人被挡在门外。
还有更小众的路线。Fossil 不用 git，分支故意难用，适合 SQLite 那种小团队；SourceHut 坚持邮件补丁；Radicle 彻底去中心化，主站挂了也能工作。
但反对方说得也实在：GitHub 不是不能忍，换的成本却看得见。有人亲眼看着项目搬走后贡献者明显变少；GitHub 的优势一直是免费和顺手，这些替代品未必给得起。
最深刻的一条评论戳破了前提：换到另一个集中式平台，只是把鸡蛋挪进另一个篮子。Git 本身就是分布式的，被集中的只有「GitHub 那一层」，这一层也该去中心化。
最实用的建议反而最朴素：把仓库同时推送到 GitHub 和别的平台，互相做镜像。谁宕机都不耽误你干活。
所以答案不是「该不该换」，而是：换去哪都治不了本，因为病根是集中本身。只要代码还挤在单一平台上，下次宕机你还会问同样的问题。

en.thesis: GitHub goes down a lot, but the real reason people stay isn't the tech — it's the community and habit.
paragraphs: GitHub has been down frequently in recent months, and someone posted asking whether to switch. The 319 comments argued back and forth, but the answers were surprisingly consistent.

One company has self-hosted GitLab for six years, saying the total downtime was just 1.5 workdays, less than GitHub's outages in the first two months. The cost was a 16GB machine, a dedicated admin, and weekly security patches.
More people recommended the lightweight options: Gitea and its fork Forgejo. They are strikingly fast, CI uses the same syntax as GitHub Actions, so migration is nearly painless.
Codeberg, a hosted service, is based on Forgejo, but it strictly forbids code that is mostly AI-generated. Some people go there for that rule, while others are kept out by it.

There are also more niche paths. Fossil doesn't use git, and branching is deliberately difficult, suited to small teams like SQLite; SourceHut insists on email patches; Radicle is fully decentralized, so it keeps working even if the main site goes down.

But the opposing side was also practical: GitHub isn't unbearable, while the cost of switching is visible. People have watched projects move away and contributors noticeably drop; GitHub's advantages have always been free and convenient, and these alternatives may not offer that.

The most insightful comment poked a hole in the premise: moving to another centralized platform is just putting eggs in a different basket. Git itself is distributed; only the 'GitHub layer' is centralized, and that layer should also be decentralized.
The most practical advice was the simplest: push your repository to GitHub and another platform at the same time, as mirrors. Then no one's outage stops your work.

So the answer isn't 'should I switch?' It's: switching anywhere won't fix the root cause, because the disease is centralization itself. As long as your code is stuck on a single platform, the next outage will have you asking the same question.

zh.thesis: 很多现在危险的地方会像摩加迪沙一样，靠监控和信息管理这类平常手段变得安全得多。
paragraphs: 摩加迪沙正在繁荣：商务部长说生意红火，26 层的 Dahab Tower 今年开业，位置离 1993 年美军士兵尸体被拖过街的地点不远。
袭击减少的原因有争议：政府归功于切断 al-Shabab；智库人士更相信监控摄像头、警察用 iPad 查车辆数据库、大批便衣特工这些平常手段。
作者想重复他的判断：许多危险地区接下来会安全得多。治安改善不需要奇迹，监控加信息管理就能带来繁荣。

en.thesis: Many dangerous places today will become much safer, the way Mogadishu did, through ordinary means like surveillance and information management.
paragraphs: Mogadishu is booming: the commerce minister says business is good, and the 26-story Dahab Tower opened this year, not far from where American soldiers' bodies were dragged through the streets in 1993.

Why the drop in attacks? The government credits cutting off al-Shabab, but think-tank analysts believe it's more the mundane tools: surveillance cameras, police using iPads to check vehicle databases, and a large network of plainclothes agents.

The author repeats his judgment: many dangerous regions will get much safer in the coming years. Improving security doesn't need miracles; surveillance plus information management can bring prosperity.

articles.title: GPT 5.6 Sol is the best "vision" model OpenAI ever released
articles.titleZh: GPT 5.6 Sol 是 OpenAI 发布过的最强「视觉」模型
articles.author: plurby

zh.thesis: Sol 是 OpenAI 迄今最强的视觉模型，但 Gemini 3.5 Flash 在检测和计数的性价比上仍更优。
paragraphs: OpenAI 上周发布 GPT-5.6 系列：Sol、Terra、Luna。Roboflow 的基准测试显示，Sol 是 OpenAI 迄今最强视觉模型，检测和计数进步明显。
检测是最大飞跃：GPT-5.5 只有 13.8 mAP@50，Sol 跳到 46.2，Terra 和 Luna 也超过 43。
但代价是速度和价格。Sol 平均每张图要 10 秒、约 2.5 美分；Luna 不到 5 秒、0.5 美分。Gemini 3.5 Flash 每张 0.8 美分，检测和计数仍领先。
还有遗留问题：超过 2000×2000 的大图上，Sol 会给出奇怪的框；OpenAI 说是低推理强度导致，只能缩图或加大推理强度，后者更慢更贵。
所以真要大规模跑检测和计数，Gemini 3.5 Flash 仍然是更省钱的选择；但 OpenAI 这次把视觉短板补上了，之后的模型值得盯。

en.thesis: Sol is OpenAI's strongest vision model yet, but Gemini 3.5 Flash still wins on cost for detection and counting.
paragraphs: OpenAI released the GPT-5.6 family last week: Sol, Terra, and Luna. Roboflow's benchmarks put Sol as the strongest vision model OpenAI has ever shipped, with clear improvements in detection and counting.
Detection is the biggest jump: GPT-5.5 scored only 13.8 mAP@50, Sol leapt to 46.2, and Terra and Luna both passed 43.

But you pay for that in speed and price. Sol averages 10 seconds per image and about 2.5 cents; Luna takes under 5 seconds at 0.5 cents. Gemini 3.5 Flash costs 0.8 cents per image and still leads on detection and counting.

There are leftover issues too: on images larger than 2000 by 2000 pixels, Sol draws odd boxes. OpenAI says it comes from low inference effort, so you have to shrink the image or raise the effort — the latter is slower and pricier.
So if you are running detection and counting at scale, Gemini 3.5 Flash remains the cheaper pick. But OpenAI has now patched its vision weakness, and the next models are worth watching.

articles.title: How a solo founder used Codex and ChatGPT to launch a fashion brand without engineers | Yana Welinder
articles.titleZh: 独立创始人如何用 Codex 和 ChatGPT 在没有工程师的情况下推出时尚品牌
articles.author: Claire Vo

zh.thesis: AI 已经能把创业所需的技术团队压缩成一个人。
paragraphs: Yana Welinder 用 AI 当联合创始人，一个人做出了时装品牌 Yana Bana。从手绘草图到 3D 打印数据，再到收款的预售网站，没有工程师参与。
关键是她把「时尚提示词」写成详细规格：轮廓、体积、面料、动感、声音全写进去。再让 Codex 帮忙操作她从没学过的 3D 设计软件，当场做出设计。
她还用 AI 做供应商调研、发邮件，甚至搭出带投票和数据库的电商站。整个流程一个人就能跑通。
所以真正重要的不是 AI 能否取代工程师，而是它把创业门槛从团队降到了个人。剩下的问题，是个人判断力能不能撑住品牌质量。

en.thesis: AI has compressed the engineering team a startup needs down to one person.
paragraphs: Yana Welinder used AI as her co-founder and built the fashion brand Yana Bana on her own. From hand-drawn sketches to 3D printing data, and then a pre-sale website that takes payments, no engineers were involved.

The key was turning her 'fashion prompts' into detailed specifications: silhouette, volume, fabric, movement, even sound, all written in. Then she got Codex to help her operate 3D design software she had never learned, and produced the designs on the spot.
She also used AI for supplier research and emails, and even built an e-commerce site with voting and a database. The whole process runs with just one person.

So the real point is not whether AI can replace engineers, but that it lowers the barrier to starting a business from a team to an individual. What's left is whether personal judgment can hold up the quality of the brand.
